transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I guess I've been doing some things at work and school lately that just don't really make sense. I work as a bookkeeping clerk, you know, mostly dealing with receipts and ledgers for this local hardware store. The store is actually right next to this amazing bakery, and they make these incredible sourdough loaves. I tried baking sourdough a couple of years ago, but my starter died after a week because my apartment is just way too drafty. The landlord refuses to fix the weather stripping on the windows. 

But anyway, at work... I've started doing this thing where I line up all the receipts across the floor. The floor there is that cheap linoleum, the kind that tries to look like real hardwood but you can tell it's fake because the grain pattern repeats every three tiles. I noticed that on my first day there. But yeah, I line the receipts up all over it, or I'll catch myself just tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Just tapping it nine times. 

Or... sometimes I'll just go over to the copier and stand there with my hands held up in the air. The copier is a Brother model, it can actually print in color but my boss only ever buys black toner because the color cartridges are a total rip-off. But I'll just stand by it with my hands up until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay. I don't really know why I'm doing it, to be honest.
When you find yourself standing with your hands in the air or tapping in sets of nine, what is going through your mind?

Well, when I'm standing there or doing the tapping... I know it sounds strange, but my mind is just racing with the numbers from work. I get completely convinced that certain invoice totals, or the account numbers, and even the due dates on the accounts are actually messages about me. 

Which reminds me, my own electric bill is always due on the 14th. It's so annoying because I get paid on the 15th, so I'm always technically a day late if I don't plan ahead. I tried calling the utility company once to change the billing cycle, but their hold music is this terrible synth jazz. It sounds exactly like this cheap Casio keyboard I had when I was eight. I used to play the little demo track on it over and over until my mom finally hid the batteries from me. 

But yeah, at the hardware store... even when my supervisor sits down with me and goes over the ledgers—his name is Dave, and he always wears these really bright Hawaiian shirts on Fridays, even when it's literally snowing outside, which is just bizarre—but even when he shows me the screen and proves that they are completely normal entries, I still can't shake it. I still feel like they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. Like the numbers are testing me or something.
Do you ever hear voices, sounds, or whispering that other people don't seem to hear?

Yeah, I actually do. Sometimes when I'm just sitting alone at my desk, or, you know, walking home from my classes... I'll hear this man's voice. He says things like, "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It's so clear that I actually stop and look around, but there's literally no one there. 

It kind of freaks me out, especially when I'm walking home. The route I take from campus goes past this really old cemetery. It's got these massive oak trees that drop acorns everywhere in the fall, and they make this loud crunching sound when you step on them. I used to collect acorns when I was a kid because my grandpa told me you could make flour out of them. He grew up on a farm in Ohio and knew all these weird survival tricks. He actually built his own tractor from scratch once. It was painted this bright, cherry red, almost like a fire engine. I always wanted to ride on it, but my mom said it was too dangerous because it didn't have seatbelts. 

But yeah, the voice... it just happens when I'm alone, and it sounds like a real person standing right next to me.

Oh, you mean like... am I stuck? No, I don't feel frozen or anything like I can't move. I could put my hands down whenever I want to, honestly. They just get kind of tired and heavy after a few minutes. 

Kind of like when I was helping my buddy move last weekend. He lives in this awful third-floor walk-up apartment, and the stairwell is incredibly narrow. We were trying to pivot this giant couch around the corner—it was this hideous crushed mustard yellow velvet. I don't even know where he got it, probably at that thrift shop on 5th Street. You know the one? It always smells faintly like mothballs and old soup. I bought a desk lamp there once, but the wiring was completely shot and it blew the fuse for half my apartment. The electrician who came out to fix it spent the whole time complaining about his son's little league baseball team. He said the kids don't even care about the game, they just want the post-game snacks. Which I totally get, because my favorite part of playing sports as a kid was always the orange slices at halftime. They were always perfectly cold in those little plastic baggies. 

But yeah, I'm not physically trapped or frozen when I stand by the copier. I just kind of do it.
Have you or others noticed you smiling, laughing, or giggling at times when nothing funny is happening, or when the situation is actually serious?

No, I haven't really noticed that, and nobody has said anything like that to me. I don't just sit there giggling to myself or anything. 

My coworker Sarah, though, she laughs at literally everything. She sits two desks down from me and watches these videos on her phone during her lunch break. I don't even use that app anymore because it was draining my battery so fast. I actually had to buy one of those portable charger blocks, but I left it on the bus last Tuesday. The bus system here is just getting worse, honestly. The drivers brake so hard that everyone goes flying forward. Once, this guy spilled his entire iced coffee all the way down the center aisle. It smelled like vanilla syrup for the rest of the ride, which normally I'd like, but it was mixed with that weird wet rubber smell the bus floors have when it rains. It made my shoes all sticky, too, and I had just bought those sneakers. They were the ones with the memory foam insoles, which are great if you're standing at the filing cabinets all day. 

But yeah, no, I don't laugh at serious stuff or just out of nowhere.
About how long have you been hearing that voice and feeling like the numbers are messages?

I'd say... maybe about eight months now? Yeah, the voices and the feeling that the numbers are messages, it's been about eight months. 

I remember because it started right around the time my sister got a new puppy. It's a Golden Retriever mix, and she named him Barnaby. He's huge now, but back then he was just this little ball of fluff. She actually brings him to my apartment sometimes, which is technically against my lease, but my landlord is never around anyway. He's this older guy who spends all his time at his cabin up north. I saw pictures of it once when I went to drop off my rent check—it's got this beautiful wraparound porch made of cedar. I love the smell of cedar. It reminds me of those little wooden blocks my grandma used to put in her closets to keep the moths away. She had this massive collection of vintage wool coats. There was this one that was bright teal with giant black buttons. I think she wore it to a parade once in the 70s. 

But yeah, it's been about eight months since all the number stuff and the voice started.
